title: Forecast‐Informed Industrial Scheduling for Air Quality, Health, and Equity Cobenefits in Developing Asia
content:
Abstract

Air pollution stemming from fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remains a major public health challenge across China, India, and Southeast Asia, especially during severe pollution episodes. Existing management strategies often rely on long-term structural reforms or short-term emergency controls, both of which can involve notable economic costs and social disruption. Here, we examined whether seasonal PM2.5 forecasts could help inform anticipatory industrial scheduling as a complementary approach to pollution mitigation. Using an integrated prediction-to-policy framework in which seasonal climate forecasts, atmospheric chemical transport modeling, and high-resolution exposure assessment are combined, we evaluated this concept within the policy context of the emission control measures implemented during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics and explored its broader regional implications through stylized scenario analysis. Under the modeled conditions, forecast-informed scheduling was associated with reductions in PM2.5 concentrations ranging from 5% to 30%. From October 2021 to February 2022, the intervention scenario was associated with an estimated 12.2% decrease in PM2.5-attributable short-term premature mortality, corresponding to 66,900 avoided deaths (95% confidence interval (CI): 46,990–86,912), and health-related economic savings of US$84.4 billion, which is equivalent to approximately 0.18% of the regional gross domestic product. The benefits were relatively balanced across income groups in China but were typically greater for lower-income populations in India and Southeast Asia during high-pollution episodes. These findings provide a regional proof of concept that seasonal environmental prediction may help inform earlier and more targeted air quality management in developing Asia, while the magnitude of the modeled benefits depends on the scenario assumptions and local implementation conditions.
